votes.reasoning: In DMGVerifier.swift:77-95 an attach that throws (for example a timeout kill) detaches whatever -mountrandom left under the private root. A plist with no mount point detaches the /dev/diskN whole disks (partitions excluded), or falls back to the leftover mounts. The detach defer runs before the root is removed. An attach that mounted nothing runs no detach. Reversal: replacing both detaches with no-ops made the tests at UpdateCheckerDownloadTests.swift:336 and :350 RED.

DMGVerifier.swift:69-95 extracts the detach loop into `detach(_:run:)`. The old defer body is moved, not duplicated, and it logs failures as before (the verdict is already decided, so a log is right). The HdiutilRunner seam has a default and exists only to make the attach-failure paths testable. runHdiutil had to become internal because Swift forbids a private default argument on an internal func. `leftoverMounts` logs its error instead of swallowing it. The `try?` in wholeDiskDevices (:139) is commented as best-effort on an already-failing path, and it reads the plist the same way mountPoint(fromAttachPlist:) already does. Minor: `dev.dropFirst("/dev/disk".count)` is computed twice at :144-145. That is not worth a round.

DMGVerifier.swift:69-95 changes only internal behavior. The HdiutilRunner seam and runHdiutil moving from private to internal (DMGVerifier.swift:160) exist for the tests. The public DMGVerifying/TeamSignatureDMGVerifier surface is unchanged. The best-effort try? in wholeDiskDevices has a justifying comment. No new process: only /usr/bin/hdiutil detach, which was already used.
